[1/1] Plan: tune Qwen2.5 0.5B on the code task with the fixed harness (device + sampling + prompt), A/B the preset against the gate baseline settings on all 136 code items, and land the measured recipe

impact_assessment.why: The gate model Qwen 0.5B baseline settings score 25.7% on code; a screen showed T=0 plus the suite prompt at 33.3% with fewer tokens, so the tuner had real headroom on a core model.
impact_assessment.benefits: Higher coding score and quality per second/GB on this machine from a measured per-model preset, without touching the baseline.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: user profile and a committed recipe; dependency: local GGUF and Vulkan; concurrency: timing under another benchmark; state: profile overwrite (backup kept)
impact_assessment.mitigation: tune through tune-run.mjs, A/B on identical load/seeds on 136 items, keep a backup, run npm test and tune:gate

checkpoints.description: [4/4] Check: tuner chose T=0 minP=.05 topP=.9 maxTokens=512 repeat=1 dry=0 newline=false topK=40, suite prompt, reasoning off. Tuner stats 35.4% vs 25.7% defaults on 48 (+9.7, b9/c23 p=.0011). 136-item A/B: 28.4% -> 33.8% (+5.4, b1/c7 p=.0703), 691 -> 537 ms (-154), 68.5 -> 59 output tokens, 128.93 -> 157.3 tok/s, memory 105,147,424 B unchanged; q/sec 0.411 -> 0.629 (+53%), q/GB +19%. npm test 606 pass/1 skip; tune:gate 9/9 ok; served on 4141 and the code request returned function add. [1/1] Plan: test whether a concise answer directive lifts SmolLM2 135M recall, then tune it through the harness and land the measured preset

impact_assessment.why: SmolLM2 recall is a gate model at 6.5% with the suite prompt; a directive screen showed the concise prompt at 13% on the 46-item rung.
impact_assessment.benefits: A measured recall gain on a core gate model without touching the baseline; the tuner picks the prompt with its own paired rule.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: user profile and a committed recipe; dependency: local GGUF on Vulkan; concurrency: other sessions loading the CPU; state: profile overwrite (backup kept)
impact_assessment.mitigation: screen with paired stats, run the tuner prompt stage on a two-candidate grid, confirm on all 65 recall items, run tests and the gate

[1/1] Plan: use the idle box to test the tuner's speed/quality choices for Qwen 0.5B; land only a load change that raises speed without quality or memory loss

impact_assessment.why: The quality and speed stages were pending and the box is finally idle; threads 12 was the tuner's fastest pick.
impact_assessment.benefits: A measured per-second improvement at identical quality and memory; confirms f16 KV and rejects a 12.6 MB context increase.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: user profile and recipe; dependency: Vulkan; concurrency: other sessions; state: profile overwrite (backups kept)
impact_assessment.mitigation: A/B on all 136 code items, pin context 4096, regenerate the recipe, run tests and the gate

[1/1] Plan: take over a home lock whose owner PID is dead, so a killed server no longer blocks the next start; keep the mtime rule for unreadable locks

impact_assessment.why: Stage 4 found a stale .lock naming a dead PID; the next start refused with already_running until the file was deleted by hand.
impact_assessment.benefits: Immediate restart after a crash or kill; no manual lock deletion.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: lock semantics; dependency: node process.kill signal 0; concurrency: a live owner replying; state: unlink race
impact_assessment.mitigation: only unlink when the file still names the judged-dead PID; treat EPERM and unreadable owners as live; add tests and a live kill/restart repro

checkpoints.description: [4/4] Check: unit tests cover dead-PID takeover and refusal to steal an unreadable fresh lock; live repro started PID 17732, killed it, confirmed the lock stayed with the dead PID, restarted (new PID 22848) and /api/health returned 200. npm test 608 pass/1 skip; tune:gate 9/9 ok. checklists: passed
Task 'stale-home-lock' completed successfully.

impact_assessment.benefits: Cold-start docs match the code; the ADR explains the ESRCH/EPERM rules and the race bound.

impact_assessment.mitigation: append ADR-087 after ADR-086, trim verbose README prose to stay under the cap, run the project check and tests

[1/1] Plan: land greedy sampling as the coder's recall preset if the full 65-item pool confirms the rung signal without losses

impact_assessment.why: The coder recall task had no current-suite preset; greedy tied the 46-item rung at 50.0 vs 47.1 (3 gains/0 losses) but that rung is too small to decide.
impact_assessment.benefits: A higher-power paired decision on the full pool; the tuner's own p<=0.2 acceptance threshold.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: user profile and committed recipe; dependency: Vulkan; concurrency: box load; state: profile overwrite (backup kept)
impact_assessment.mitigation: re-measure both arms on all 65 items with the same load; refuse to write unless p<=0.2 and gains exceed losses; run tests and the gate
